newsitem.title: CANADA: Albert Farm Income Disaster Program extended.
newsitem.headline: Albert Farm Income Disaster Program extended.

text.p: Alberta's provincial government said on Wednesday that farmers now have until the end of September to apply for its Farm Income Disaster Program.
"It's been a late season in some areas and it's been unusually wet in others, putting farmers well behind in their field operations," Alberta Agriculture Minister Ed Stelmach said in a statement.
The deadline was extended to September 30 from July 31.
"As a result, many farmers and their accountants, have been telling us they need more time to prepare their application forms," Stelmach added.
The FDIP was introduced in the 1995 tax year. The program paid out C$63.3 million in fiscal 1996 to 4,943 applicants.
